title: VPC Migration Planner with Preflight/Postflight Hooks and Staged Rollout
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Scope: build a migration planning and execution tool for Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) that orchestrates version rollouts, coordinates stateful schema migrations, and provides preflight/postflight validation hooks. This ticket covers the planner and control-plane components that produce an execution plan, the hook API for customers to provide custom checks, and a safe staged rollout sequencer that integrates with LTS channels and rollout gates.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic, idempotent migration plans for Private clusters across LTS channels.
- Support dry-run simulations and a rich preflight phase that emits actionable failures before any destructive step.
- Allow staged rollouts including canary fleets, automated metrics-based progression, and fast rollback on regressions.
- Integrate with our runtime to coordinate in-memory cache drains, KV cache warmup, and model-serving compatibility checks.
- Minimize customer downtime for common schema changes via online-compatible migration patterns and safe write/reads modes.

Design notes and constraints:
- Planner will produce a sequence of steps tagged with: component, stage (preflight/check/migrate/postflight), expected duration, and idempotency token. Steps are declarative JSON but execution is driven by the Private control-plane agent.
- Preflight hooks: HTTP/GRPC callback interface customers can implement to validate tenant-specific assumptions (disk, custom KMS, network egress rules). Hooks have a timeout and can be retried. Failure modes are safe-fail (abort) or advisory depending on gate configuration.
- Postflight validations: schema checksums, canary traffic acceptance tests, integration smoke tests (example: embedder/encoder compatibility).
- Rollout gates: metric thresholds (error rate, p95 latency, token-cost variance) read from customer dashboards or default SLOs; gates support manual approvals, automatic progression, or rollback triggers.
- Versioning & LTS channels: planner understands channel constraints (e.g., only allow major upgrades on LTS-eligible clusters), maps model/runtime compatibility matrices, and can select compatible JVM/KV/driver artifacts.
- Migration types supported initially: non-blocking online schema changes, transactional table copy + swap, and migration jobs for large stateful stores. Dangerous/irreversible migrations require explicit admin confirmation and an extended canary.
- Rollback strategy: point-in-time snapshots for data stores where possible; for incompatible schema changes, provide a documented backward-compatibility migration path. Abort guarantees: the planner must leave the cluster in a well-defined, documented state.
- Observability: emit structured events for every plan step (plan.start, step.start, step.end, step.fail) with trace IDs for cross-cluster correlation. Expose a per-plan dashboard in Console with token-level cost estimate, estimated downtime, and rollback options.
- Telemetry & audits: all plan executions must be recorded to customer audit logs with actor, time, and commit id.

Non-goals: automated conversion of arbitrary customer schema; we will provide tools and templates but not auto-translate business logic.

Acceptance criteria and validation are separate fields. Implementation will include unit tests for the planner, an e2e staging test harness, and a migration-sim dry-run mode in Private clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Planner can generate an idempotent execution plan for a sample minor and patch upgrade in a VPC test cluster.
Preflight hook API implemented; sample hook confluence doc and example implementation in the reference repo; failures surface in Console with remediation hints.
Staged rollout sequencer supports canary -> ramp -> full progression controlled by metric thresholds and manual approval.
Postflight validations run automatically and mark the plan as successful only if all validations pass; failures trigger rollback or pause according to gate config.
Telemetry events emitted for every step and visible in Console tracing for a completed plan.
Dry-run mode simulates the full plan without applying destructive changes and produces a remediation checklist when issues are found.
Integration tests exercising online schema migration patterns show zero 5xx increase in canary fleets during ingestions at 50% traffic.
Security review completed and documented for hook endpoints, agent credentials, and KMS interactions.
Migration rollouts are compatible with LTS channel constraints and documented in the release notes for private-2026.04.
